title: Curvature, and a triangle on a sphere
lede: Surfaces are colored by Gaussian curvature K: red where positive, gray where zero, blue where negative. On the sphere, grow a triangle bounded by great-circle arcs and read its angles.
notice: The sphere is curved the same way everywhere (K > 0), the cylinder has K = 0 and can be unrolled flat, the saddle has K < 0 everywhere. The torus has all three kinds of point.
On the sphere, the angles of a triangle always add up to more than 180 degrees.
The excess over 180 degrees, in radians, equals the triangle's area on the unit sphere. The area is computed separately, by a different formula.
hint: Drag to rotate. Choose a surface; on the sphere, slide the triangle size.
